title: Article 73 — Extent of executive power of the Union

content.overview: Article 73 provides that the executive power of the Union extends to (a) matters with respect to which Parliament has power to make laws; and (b) the exercise of such rights, authority and jurisdiction as are exercisable by the Government of India by virtue of any treaty or agreement — subject to the provisions of the Constitution. On matters in the Concurrent List, the Union’s executive power does not extend in a State to matters with respect to which the State Legislature also has power, unless the Constitution or Parliament by law otherwise provides. Until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the Union’s executive power also extends to giving directions to States as specified and to matters on which the Dominion had power under pre-Constitution arrangements as continued.
content.glance: Union executive power co-extensive with Parliament’s legislative power + treaty/agreement rights. Concurrent List: Union executive in States only if Constitution/Parliament so provides.
content.study:
Article 73 extent:
(1)(a) Matters with respect to which Parliament may make laws.
(1)(b) Rights, authority and jurisdiction under treaty or agreement.

Proviso: Concurrent List — Union executive power does not, save as Constitution or Parliament by law provides, extend in a State to matters on which the State Legislature also has power.

Examination: co-extensivity with Union legislative competence; treaty jurisdiction; Concurrent List limitation; contrast Art 162 (State executive extent).

sections.heading: Extent
sections.body:
1. Matters within Parliament’s legislative competence.
2. Treaty/agreement rights and jurisdiction of the Government of India.
3. Concurrent List in a State: Union executive only if Constitution or parliamentary law so provides.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the extent of the executive power of the Union under Article 73?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 73, the executive power of the Union extends to matters with respect to which Parliament has power to make laws, and to rights, authority and jurisdiction exercisable by the Government of India under any treaty or agreement. On Concurrent List matters, the Union’s executive power does not extend in a State to matters on which the State Legislature also has power, unless the Constitution or Parliament by law otherwise provides.

examTips: Co-extensive with Parliament’s law-making power; Concurrent List limit in States.

keyTakeaways: Art 73: extent of Union executive power; Concurrent List caveat.
